issues.legal_issue: Statutory boards and development authorities that allot sites while undertaking development are subject to consumer-forum jurisdiction for alleged deficiency in the services they provide.
material_facts: The appellant was a statutory marketing board that allotted plots for use in a grain market.
The allottees complained that the plots could not be used for the intended business because the market area had not been developed and necessary facilities were lacking.
The appellant disputed that the allottees were consumers, although it had not challenged the consumer forum’s jurisdiction below.
issues.conclusion: Statutory boards and development authorities that allot sites with a promise of development are amenable to consumer-forum jurisdiction in cases alleging deficiency of service.
issues.legal_principle: The broad meanings of “consumer” and “service” under the Consumer Protection Act, including Section 2(1)(o), encompass development and allotment services by statutory authorities. The Court relied on U.T. Chandigarh Administration v. Amarjeet Singh, Karnataka Industrial Areas and Development Board v. Nandi Cold Storage Pvt. Ltd., Narne Construction (P) Ltd. v. Union of India, and Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta.

rule.if: consumer_service_complaint and service_deficiency_alleged and (statutory_site_allotment or development_service_promised)

predicates.consumer_service_complaint: An allottee brought a complaint before a consumer forum concerning services connected with an allotted site.
predicates.service_deficiency_alleged: The allottee alleged that the provider failed to perform a service connected with the site.
predicates.statutory_site_allotment: A statutory body allotted the site.
predicates.development_service_promised: The provider allotted the site while undertaking or promising development.

issues.definition: When a consumer-service complaint alleges deficient services connected with a statutory site allotment or promised development, the consumer forum has jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: An authority that allots plots for a specified business use must facilitate their use for that purpose, and prolonged failure to provide necessary facilities that prevents the intended use constitutes deficient service.
material_facts: The plots were allotted for auctioning and trading in grain, rather than through a free auction or on an “as is where is” basis.
The allottees could not conduct the intended grain business because necessary market facilities were lacking.
The appellant had failed to develop the area adequately for more than a decade, preventing the allottees from carrying on the intended business.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s prolonged inaction in providing the facilities needed for the intended grain business constituted deficiency of service, even though providing amenities was not a condition precedent under the allotment letters.
issues.legal_principle: A service provider must facilitate the utilization and enjoyment of allotted plots for the purpose for which they were allotted. The Court applied Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh v. Shantikunj Investment (P) Ltd. and Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board v. Raj Pal, and referred to U.T. Chandigarh Administration v. Amarjeet Singh. It also recognized that providing amenities need not be a condition precedent to the allotment for an obligation to provide necessary facilities to arise.

rule.if: specified_business_use and development_stage_allotment and essential_facilities_absent and inability_to_use_for_intended_business

predicates.specified_business_use: The provider allotted the site for a particular business use.
predicates.development_stage_allotment: The site was allotted while development of the area was still underway.
predicates.essential_facilities_absent: Facilities needed for the intended business were not provided.
predicates.inability_to_use_for_intended_business: The absence of facilities prevented the allottee from carrying on the intended business.

issues.definition: If a site is allotted during development for a specified business use and missing essential facilities prevent that use, the provider’s failure to facilitate it is deficient service.

issues.legal_issue: Allottees remain obliged to pay instalments under their allotment terms, but a provider’s failure to supply necessary facilities may justify proportionate relief from penal interest and other charges.
material_facts: The allottees did not pay the instalments required by their allotment letters, relying on the absence of necessary market facilities.
The allottees were incorrect in refusing to pay the instalments and thereby breached the payment terms.
The appellant had failed to develop the area for more than two decades, causing loss to the allottees and preventing the intended business.
The consumer fora granted relief on interest and charges, and the Supreme Court found that relief adequate in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The allottees were not entitled to withhold instalments, but proportionate relief from penal interest and other charges was justified by the prolonged failure to provide facilities; the relief granted by the consumer fora was adequate and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Instalments are payable as part of the allotment contract, and allottees cannot postpone payment merely because some amenities are missing. However, under Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh v. Shantikunj Investment (P) Ltd., relief proportionate to missing facilities may be granted concerning penalty and penal interest. U.T. Chandigarh Administration v. Amarjeet Singh explained that relief depends on the circumstances, and Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board v. Raj Pal applied those principles and distinguished the treatment of simple interest from penal and compound interest.

rule.if: allotment_payment_dispute and installments_unpaid and essential_facilities_unprovided and prolonged_development_failure

predicates.allotment_payment_dispute: A dispute arose over payments required under terms for an allotted site.
predicates.installments_unpaid: The allottees failed to pay instalments required by their allotment terms.
predicates.essential_facilities_unprovided: The provider had not supplied facilities needed to use the site as intended.
predicates.prolonged_development_failure: The provider’s failure to develop the area and provide facilities continued for a prolonged period.

issues.definition: When instalments remain unpaid despite a prolonged failure to provide essential facilities, the instalments remain due but proportionate relief from penal charges may be granted.
